t: #3591 Check if Any Element Has Prime Frequency
o: Count how often each value appears and report whether any frequency is a prime number. Frequencies are at most 100, so primality can be checked by trial division up to sqrt(frequency). Examples: [1,2,3,4,5,4] has frequency 2 for value 4 (prime, true); all-distinct arrays give frequency 1 (not prime, false).
k: Frequency counting with a hash map is the whole problem.
Frequencies are <= 100, so trial division is more than fast enough for the primality test.

a.i: Tally frequencies, then test each frequency for primality with the classic O(sqrt(f)) loop. Frequency 1 is not prime, matching example 2.
s: Build a frequency counter of nums.
For each frequency f, check primality by trial division from 2 to sqrt(f).
Return true if any frequency is prime.
a.t: O(n + F * sqrt(F)) where F <= n is the max frequency — effectively O(n).

w: Straightforward counting problem; the only trap is treating 1 as prime. A follow-up might ask for the count of elements with prime frequency or use much larger values (then sieve or Miller-Rabin).
